items.title: Australian couple trapped in Argentina with no legal rights to biological child
items.description: Jonathan and Amy had a child via surrogacy in Argentina. They have been stuck there for 12 months, unable to bring their daughter home.

items.title: How Australia has the power to ban 'ISIS brides' from returning
items.description: One of the Australian women being held in a Syrian refugee camp has been barred from returning home after being given a temporary exclusion order — but the ban may not be as temporary as the name implies.

items.title: Hanson plays into meme status, Taylor goes on tour
items.description: This week the new opposition leader revealed his shadow cabinet while Pauline Hanson spun through a cycle she knows well.

items.title: Extremist material allegedly found on man's phone after vehicle stop
items.description: A 31-year-old has been arrested a second time after police stopped and searched a vehicle in Yagoona and seized three mobile phones allegedly storing violent extremist material.

items.title: In her memoir, Gisèle Pelicot reveals the man she kept hidden
items.description: The world knows Gisèle Pelicot as the woman who waived anonymity during France's most infamous rape trial. But in her new memoir she reveals an unexpected story — the boyfriend she kept hidden and the love that helped her face an open courtroom.

items.title: SA secures Australian MotoGP, world-first street circuit announced
items.description: The South Australian government has confirmed the Australian MotoGP will move to Adelaide from 2027, bringing with it huge economic benefits, but the opposition and Greens say the state has other priorities.

items.title: Unemployment rate remains at 4.1pc, leading to talk of another rate rise
items.description: Australia's unemployment rate remained at 4.1 per cent in January, with 17,800 more employed people.

items.title: How the deadliest avalanche in the US in 40 years unfolded
items.description: An avalanche in California has left eight back-country skiers dead and one missing. Here's how it unfolded.

items.title: Australian-first remotely piloted police drone trial raises surveillance questions
items.description: Police will control drones from more than 600 kilometres away from a rural town battling high crime rates.

items.title: Hate laws put free speech at risk, constitutional expert tells inquiry
items.description: An influx of federal and state laws trying to curb hateful rhetoric after a wave of antisemitic attacks are risking free speech and could anger the public, a constitutional law expert warns.

items.title: Charlie Pickering on his ADHD, satire and the 'ludicrous' Trump era
items.description: Political satire occasionally comes at a price, but Charlie Pickering still believes the right joke at the right time can have a huge impact.

items.title: 'Ten hours of hell': Rugby fans' fury amid World Cup ticket crashes
items.description: Rugby fans from around the world are furious after failing to get tickets to the 2027 Men's World Cup due technical glitches and website crashes.

items.title: Senate committee features climate disinformation and Dr Karl's clash with One Nation
items.description: The scourge of AI-slopaganda, viral disinformation campaigns and online attacks against individuals and institutions is going to get far worse before it gets better, if the latest public hearings on the topic are any indication.

items.title: Ukraine recaptures territory amid 'extraordinary' Russian casualties
items.description: Ukraine has made its largest battlefield gains in more than two and a half years, retaking more than 200 square kilometres of its territory from Russia in just five days, according to a new analysis.

items.title: Young victims face meth-fuelled driver who struck them outside Canberra school
items.description: Tayler Hazell is facing his victims in a sentencing hearing in the ACT Supreme Court. He struck two students in Canberra in a stolen car while high on drugs.

items.title: Live: ASX follows Wall Street higher, unemployment steady
items.description: While the unemployment rate remains steady, the ASX opened strongly on the back of a batch of solid results. Follow the day's events and insights from our business reporters on the ABC News live markets blog.

items.title: Best International Film Oscar-hopefuls finally hit Australian cinemas
items.description: Australians will also finally be able to catch Sirât and The Voice of Hind Rajab, two movies that will be vying for Best International Film at the Academy Awards next month.

items.title: A heartwarming tribute for 'a great human'
items.description: This Winter Olympics aerials competition saw plenty of Aussies achieve lifetime goals, but they never forgot the one person who was missing.

items.title: Rescues and highway closures amid north Queensland rains
items.description: Heavy rainfall across north Queensland has led to multiple rescues and the closure of several sections of the Bruce Highway.

items.title: Man allegedly compiled reports for 'Chinese intelligence', court hears
items.description: A LinkedIn introduction led to Australian businessman Alexander Csergo compiling reports for two people he believed worked for a Chinese intelligence agency in exchange for cash, a jury has heard.

items.title: Premier weighs in after two hospital escapees allegedly kill three people
items.description: NSW Premier Chris Minns says it is "deeply distressing" that two mental health patients who escaped from the same Sydney hospital within 24 hours went on to allegedly kill three people between them.

items.title: Adelaide Ice Arena charged after patrons hospitalised for alleged carbon monoxide exposure
items.description: Safework SA has launched criminal proceedings against the Adelaide Ice Arena, after hockey players and spectators were allegedly exposed to "significant levels" of carbon monoxide more than two years ago, leading to more than 40 hospitalisations.

items.title: Alcoa's green efforts dubbed 'disappointing' by WA premier after $55m payment
items.description: Roger Cook criticises Alcoa's environmental record for being "not at the level we expect", after the US mining giant agreed to pay $55 million for clearing a native jarrah forest in WA's south without approval.

items.title: The 'rarely spoken about' reason many women are leaving footy clubs
items.description: The women's team from Kyneton's 15-month public and bitter saga suggests it is the canary in the coal mine of a widespread issue for women's players across the country.

items.title: Woman finds Antarctic pioneer's unmarked grave in Melbourne
items.description: Captain John King Davis was one of Australia's greatest Antarctic explorers, but for decades, his final resting place was an unmarked grave in Melbourne. Today, that will change.
